title: CrossModal Study
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from a crossmodal target-discrimination study investigating attentional preparation and alpha oscillations. Participants were cued to attend to auditory, visual, or non-specific targets, with frequency-tagged stimuli (36 Hz visual, 40 Hz auditory) presented during a preparatory interval preceding target onset. The study examines how cross-modal attention and target expectation modulate neural oscillatory activity and behavioral performance.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from healthy adult participants performing a cued target-discrimination task with auditory and visual targets and distractors. An additional EOG channel was used to monitor eye activity. During the cue-target interval, a frequency-tagged fixation cross (36 Hz) and an amplitude-modulated tone (40 Hz) were presented. Participants indicated target identity via keyboard arrow presses across 28 experimental blocks. Two participants were excluded due to task abortion or below-chance performance. Data were collected at the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom.
